gap: No result ChatGPT got states how many hours each 3,000 Wh station carries a refrigerator-sized load once the station's own measured idle draw (8 W to 37 W, The Solar Lab) is counted: about 56 h for the Jackery HomePower 3000, 46 h for the BLUETTI Elite 300 and 33 h for the Pecron F3000LFP at a 41 W average load.
standout_why: I opened six of the result pages: powerstations.reviews/jackery-3000, wattpowerstation's home-backup guide, thesolarlab's big-stations roundup, powersized/reviews, lightsonlabs and power-verdict's best-3000Wh guide. None gives an idle-draw figure for any of these five units; thesolarlab's roundup has idle only for the Apex 300 and F3800 Plus. powerstations.reviews computes fridge hours as rated Wh × 0.85 ÷ 41 W (about 63 h for the HomePower 3000) with no idle term, and ChatGPT's answer only says low loads 'can shorten those estimates'. wattpowerstation already has tested usable Wh and $ per usable Wh for the Jackery, Pecron and Anker (not the Elite 300), so cost per usable Wh alone would rate 1. Not opened: thepowerstationreport, Good Housekeeping, wattpowerstation's /power-stations/ page and the uncited results; jackery.com returned 429. The score assumes those lack it too.
decides: On the page's own line (a fridge, lights and internet through a two-day outage) the Jackery HomePower 3000 is confirmed as the pick: it is the only one of the five that holds a 41 W average load for 48 h (about 56 h). The BLUETTI Elite 300 is second at about 46 h, ahead of the Anker F3000 (42 h), EcoFlow DELTA 3 Ultra (40 h) and Pecron F3000LFP (33 h), so it honestly takes the lower-price segment at about $0.42 per usable Wh on its store price. The Pecron's low price per Wh does not carry over to low-load outage use: its 37 W idle draw takes about 58% of the battery over 48 h. All idle figures come from one reviewer, The Solar Lab, and its Jackery and Elite 300 pages do not state that the inverter was on.

findings.label: Share of the battery the idle draw takes over a 48 h outage
findings.source_title: The Solar Lab reviews (idle figures per product above)
findings.note: Idle W × 48 h ÷ rated Wh, e.g. 37 × 48 = 1,776 Wh ÷ 3,072 = 57.8%. Assumes the inverter stays on for the whole outage, as it must for a fridge that cycles.

findings.label: Hours carrying a 41 W average fridge load, idle draw included
findings.value: Jackery about 56 h; Elite 300 about 46 h; Anker about 42 h; EcoFlow about 40 h; Pecron about 33 h

findings.note: Usable Wh ÷ (41 W + idle W): 2,759 ÷ 49 = 56.3; 2,592 ÷ 56 = 46.3; 2,580 ÷ 61.5 = 42.0; 2,519 ÷ 63 = 40.0; 2,550 ÷ 78 = 32.7. The 41 W fridge average is this rival page's input, which gives about 63 h for the Jackery with no idle term. First-order estimate; Dealectric has not tested it.
